subject: Skyline — post-call technical alignment & next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@skyline-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-10-03T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — Skyline product search experiment (post-call recap)

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have the same priorities captured.

Key pain points you shared:
- Peak latency spikes during promos: p95 approaching 1.1s for search rerank and p99 > 2s; customer conversion drop observed at >1s.
- High variance in input length: product descriptions + reviews mean many requests require ~4–8k token context.
- Cost sensitivity for high-throughput endpoints (holiday window) while preserving model quality for long-context ranking.

Goals you prioritized:
- Target p50 < 250ms, p95 < 800ms for production rerank workload at steady-state; acceptable warm p95 up to 1.2s during cold starts.
- Sustained throughput target ~100–150 req/s for core region (US-EAST) with burst handling to 400 req/s for 10–30 minute windows.
- Support for long-context scoring (up to 8k tokens) with preservation of precision on top-k ranking.

Technical constraints / preferences:
- Prefer open weights that can be quantized (instruction-tuned Llama-family variant was mentioned).
- Customer must retain control over audit logs and key material; consider Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering.
- EU data residency not required initially, but later expansion likely.

Initial topology sketch we discussed:
- Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) for steady-state rerank traffic to provide predictable p95 SLOs and KV cache persistence.
- Hosted fallback pool (shared capacity) for elastic bursts and canary traffic.
- Prefix/KV caching for common catalog context + continuous batching window tuned to 20–40ms to balance latency vs token-efficiency.
- Model variants: primary large model (quantized 4-bit, 8k context) + fallback smaller low-latency model for degraded mode.

Deliverables / next steps:
1) Redwood to produce a one-page architecture sketch + capacity estimate (attached: skyline_solution_sketch.pdf).
2) Draft SLA and cost estimate for Dedicated + burst overflow (attached: initial_sla_estimate.xlsx).
3) Security questionnaire and SOC2 excerpt — Alex, please confirm the right contact on your side to receive these.
4) Technical deep-dive with your infra and ML platforms teams next week to validate KV cache semantics and batching windows (30–45m).

Proposed times: Thu 2027-10-06 10:00–10:45 PT or Fri 2027-10-07 09:00–09:45 PT. Which works best?

Thanks — I’ll sync with Ben and Mina to finalize the sketch and capacity numbers before the call.

Cheers,

--
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — helpful summary and good alignment on targets. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Peak burst profile: our telemetry shows holiday peaks last ~20 minutes and are very spiky. For the burst plan, can you share how fast fallback routing would occur (seconds vs minutes) and whether pre-warming is supported?

2) Security: we need the SOC2 excerpt and the KMS/HSM integration details. Please route those to procurement@skyline-retail.com and cc me.

3) Measurement: when you propose p95 < 800ms, is that measured at Redwood API ingress or end-to-end including our frontend proxy? We’d prefer both variants documented for the SLA.

Availability: Thu 10/6 10:00 PT works for the deep-dive; I’ll invite our infra and ML infra owners.

Appreciate the attachments — I’ll review and follow up with Samir on the contract path.

—Alex

Skyline Retail

Nice recap. A couple of operational notes to prepare for the deep-dive: 

- Owner assignments: Ben (sales lead) / Priyom (solution engineering) / Mina (inference runtime & quantization).
- Pre-warm strategy: Dedicated pools can be warmed to pinned model state; hosted fallback supports cold-starts with model warmers (we can target <45s cold-start for 8k models with optimized kernels).
- Routing behavior: smart routing can flip to fallback within one request window if capacity is saturated (practical observed failover latency: single-digit ms for routing decision, model warm-up depends on pre-warm state).
- Measurement: we track both ingress and end-to-end in the Console; SLAs we show are ingress p95 but we can publish an E2E addendum.

I’ll prepare a short ops checklist for the meeting outlining what we’ll need from Skyline infra (VPC peering info, allowed CIDR ranges, IAM role for auditing). Priyom / Mina, can you add runtime-level notes to the sketch (batching window numbers and KV cache TTL defaults)?

Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
